theme: per-person UI state (selection) is cleared when a regeneration is DISPATCHED, not when the new graph ARRIVES, so an index chosen during the async window is applied to a different, possibly smaller roster
summary: App.tsx calls resetSelection() before bg.generate(), but generation is asynchronous. Any person selected while "Generating…" is showing survives into the replacement view. PersonPanel then calls eccentricity(graph, index) during render; the core throws for an out-of-range vertex, and there is no error boundary (main.tsx renders <App/> bare), so React unmounts the whole UI and the organizer loses the roster. The .busy overlay (app.css:218) blocks the mouse but sets no inert/aria-hidden, so every buddy-list row, the search combobox and the graph nodes stay focusable and Enter-activatable; under @media (max-width:820px) `main { overflow:auto }` also puts the list outside the overlay's box, making it mouse-reachable. usePathFinder has the analogous guard (a >= graph.n) and degrades to a blank Path panel instead — the same root cause with a softer symptom.
failure: Reproduced through the real App with the appErrorRecovery worker harness: generate an 8-person roster and deliver the result; click "Edit people", set the roster to 5 names, click Generate (status becomes running, selection cleared); while running click the buddy-list row for person 8 (PersonPanel opens for "H"); deliver generateResult(5, 4, {seed:1}). Render throws `Error: vertex 7 must be an integer in [0, 4]` at src/panels/PersonPanel.tsx:41 and the app unmounts. No test in the 249-test suite selects a person during an in-flight generation, so the suite stays green.
remediation: Clear (or clamp) the transient per-person state when the VIEW is replaced, not when generation is dispatched — e.g. an effect in App keyed on the view identity that runs resetSelection(), or have useBuddyGraph's view swap drive it. Belt-and-braces: make PersonPanel refuse to render for an index outside 0..view.names.length-1 rather than letting a core range error escape a render, and/or block keyboard reach into <main> while the busy overlay is up (inert).
invariant: For every render, every index held in transient per-person state is inside the current view: selected === null || selected < view.names.length, hovered === null || hovered < view.names.length, and (path.ends === null || both ends < view.names.length). Equivalently: no core query is ever called with a vertex outside 0..graph.n-1.

theme: a displayed count conflates two different outcomes, so the app states something false about the rules the user just wrote
summary: resolveNamedPairs returns `dropped = named.length - pairs.length`, which includes rules removed by dedupePairs (an (a,b)/(b,a) restatement of the same rule) and self-pairs, not just rules naming somebody the roster no longer has. RosterModal renders that number as "N buddy rule(s) doesn't/don't match anyone in this roster and won't be used" — false on both halves for a de-duplicated rule: it matches, and it IS used.
failure: Rendered RosterModal with roster [Alice, Ben, Chloe, Dev, Eve, Fran]; added rule 1 = Alice/Ben required and rule 2 = Ben/Alice required. The note "1 buddy rule doesn't match anyone in this roster and won't be used." appears, and clicking Generate still passes [{a:0,b:1,kind:"required"}] — so the rule both matches and is applied. Same false note for a single row Ben/ben (self-pair). The existing test (constraints.test.ts "de-duplicates, counting the collapse") pins dropped===1 and therefore locks the wrong number in.
remediation: Return the two outcomes separately — e.g. { pairs, unresolved, deduped } where `unresolved` counts only named pairs that fail to resolve to two distinct roster indices — and word the note from `unresolved` (optionally mentioning collapsed duplicates as a distinct, non-alarming line).
invariant: The count RosterModal presents as "doesn't match anyone in this roster" equals exactly |{ p in named : indexOf(p.a) === undefined || indexOf(p.b) === undefined || indexOf(p.a) === indexOf(p.b) }| for all (named, names) — it never counts a pair that resolved successfully and appears in `pairs`.

theme: the test sources are outside every static gate, so a test can silently drift from the component contract it claims to cover
summary: tsconfig.json has "include": ["src", "vite.config.ts"], so `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit && vite build) never look at app/test. A real type error is already sitting there, and the prop it concerns is F10's entry point from the explorer, which consequently has no test at all.
failure: `npx tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --strict --jsx react-jsx ... test/explorer.test.tsx` reports: test/explorer.test.tsx(47,6): error TS2741: Property 'onFindPath' is missing ... but required in type 'Props'. The suite is green because vitest transpiles without typechecking. Grepping test/ for "Find a path"/onFindPath returns nothing, so PersonPanel's route-start button — the only way a user starts a path from the explorer — is exercised by no test, and removing/renaming the prop turns nothing red.
remediation: Add a test tsconfig (or extend include to ["src", "test", "vite.config.ts"]) and wire it into the typecheck script so tsc covers the suite; fix the missing onFindPath prop and add a test that clicks "Find a path from here" and asserts the pending-pick state.
invariant: `npm run typecheck` at app/ type-checks every .ts/.tsx file under app/ (src and test alike) and exits non-zero on any error — i.e. no source file the test runner transpiles is outside the typechecker's include set.

theme: a per-render helper rebuilds a whole-roster index once per rule row, so editor render cost is rows x roster instead of rows + roster
summary: resolvePerson calls indexByName(names), building a fresh Map over the entire roster, on every invocation. ConstraintsEditor calls it twice per rule row on every render (and the rows render whether the <details> is open or not), so the roster index is rebuilt 2 x pairs.length times per keystroke anywhere in the modal.
failure: Measured in-repo: 400 resolvePerson calls against a 1000-name roster took 65 ms (vitest, node). That is the per-render cost at the documented ceilings (MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS = 200 rows, MAX_ROSTER_N = 1000 names) — ~65 ms of main-thread work for every character typed in the roster textarea or any rule field, on the same render path the file's own comments optimise elsewhere (datalist instead of per-row selects, chosen precisely to avoid ceiling-scale cost).
remediation: Build the name index once per render in ConstraintsEditor (useMemo on `names`) and have the rows consult that map, keeping resolvePerson as the single-shot convenience over it — or memoise indexByName on the names array identity.
invariant: For all (names, pairs), one render of ConstraintsEditor constructs the roster name index a number of times independent of pairs.length (O(1) constructions), so total unknown-name resolution work is O(names.length + pairs.length), not O(names.length x pairs.length).

theme: attacker-sized pasted text multiplied by roster size does synchronous main-thread work with no cap
summary: `fuzzyMatch` normalizes the QUERY (`query.trim().toLowerCase()`) inside itself, and `rankMatches` calls it once per roster name, so a search does O(|query| x names.length) character copies before any matching. The query is an uncapped controlled `<input>` (`PersonSearch`, no maxLength, no debounce, no length gate), so a paste sizes the multiplier. The early-exit in the subsequence loop does not help: the normalization is paid unconditionally per name, even for a query that matches nothing. This is the one place in the app where a size gate is simply absent — every other superlinear surface (file bytes, roster chars, import n, import density, constraint pairs, force ticks, polish) has one.
failure: Reproduced by rendering `PersonSearch` with 1000 names (the app's own ceiling) and firing one change event: a 4,000,000-char value blocks the main thread for 3038 ms, and the NEXT keystroke costs another 2935 ms. Direct `rankMatches` timings on the same 1000 names: 500 K chars 366 ms, 2 M 1345 ms, 8 M 6178 ms — linear in |query| x names. An equivalent loop with the normalization hoisted out of the per-name call runs the 2 M case in 4 ms, confirming the per-candidate normalization is the whole cost.
remediation: Normalize the query once in `rankMatches` and pass the normalized string to the matcher (split `fuzzyMatch` into a pre-normalized inner function, or normalize at the call site). Additionally short-circuit: a query longer than the longest name can never be a subsequence of any name, so return `[]` without touching candidates; and cap the stored query length in `PersonSearch` the way `RosterModal.capText` caps the roster text, so the DOM/state cost is bounded too.
invariant: For all `names` and all `query`, the running time of `rankMatches(query, names, limit)` is bounded by O(|query| + sum of |name|) — i.e. the cost of a fixed query must not scale with `names.length` beyond the per-name matching itself. Machine-checkable as a ratio with no case table: for any large L, elapsed(rankMatches(q of length L, names of length N)) must be within a small constant factor (e.g. 4x) of elapsed(rankMatches(same q, names of length 1)); equivalently, instrument and assert the query is normalized exactly once per `rankMatches` call regardless of `names.length`.

theme: per-keystroke superlinear main-thread work in the roster modal at the app's own documented caps
summary: Each rule row validates its two fields with `resolvePerson(p.a, names)` / `resolvePerson(p.b, names)`, and `resolvePerson` builds a fresh `indexByName(names)` Map over the ENTIRE roster on every call (app/src/constraints.ts:153-157). At the app's own caps (1000 names, MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS = 200) that is 400 full O(n) map builds — 400,000 Map inserts — per render, and the editor re-renders on every keystroke in the roster textarea (the `parsed.names` identity changes) and on every keystroke in any rule field. The same render also pays `resolveNamedPairs` (one more index build) and `validateDetailed`'s O(n^2) prohibited-pair connectivity walk once per keystroke when any "never buddies" rule exists. Rule-field inputs are also uncapped, so a large paste into one adds an O(|text|) trim/lowercase per render on top. Both caps are reachable without typing: import a file with 1000 people and 200 rules, then press "Edit people".
failure: Measured on the real components. Isolated: 400 `resolvePerson` calls over 1000 names = 71 ms of pure JS. `validateDetailed` at n=1000 with a prohibited pair = 16-24 ms (0.7 ms with none). End-to-end through `RosterModal` (jsdom) with a 1000-name roster, one keystroke in the textarea: 31-40 ms with 0 rules vs 166-200 ms with 200 rules — a ~130 ms marginal cost per keystroke that recurs for every character typed. No freeze, but sustained typing at the documented maximum is continuously janky, and the cost is quadratic in the two knobs an imported file controls.
remediation: Build the roster lookup once per render (e.g. `useMemo(() => indexByName(names), [names])` in `ConstraintsEditor`, passing the map to a `resolvePersonIn(map, text)` helper, keeping `resolvePerson` as a thin wrapper for other callers). Reuse that one map in `resolveNamedPairs` as well, and consider memoizing/deferring the `ruleProblems` `validateDetailed` pass so the O(n^2) walk is not re-run on every roster keystroke. Cap rule-field input length like `capText` does for the roster.
invariant: For all `names` and all `pairs`, rendering `ConstraintsEditor` constructs the roster name index O(1) times (independent of `pairs.length`); total resolution work is O(names.length + sum of row text lengths), never O(names.length x pairs.length). Machine-checkable as a cost ratio with no case table: for a fixed roster, (render time with R rule rows - render time with 0 rule rows) must not grow with `names.length`; or instrument `indexByName` and assert its call count per render is independent of `pairs.length`.

theme: ConstraintKind is a closed union but its consumers branch on it with if/else and a ternary instead of an exhaustive switch, so it silently misroutes rather than fails to compile when a third kind is added — and F9 (the actually-next-committed feature) needs exactly a third kind
summary: ConstraintKind consumers (RosterModal.tsx:94's if/else, constraints.ts:57's ternary in splitPairs) are non-exhaustive, unlike every other discriminated union in this codebase (GraphCanvas.positionsFor, highlight.ts's nodeClass/edgeClass, constraintMessages.ts's describeReason), all of which use assertNever or a bare switch under noImplicitReturns so a missed case fails the build.
failure: F9's 'previous edges become soft-required' is the minimal-diff fit for the existing NamedPair/ConstraintPair machinery (toNamedPairs/resolveNamedPairs already solve exactly the roster-churn/index-drift problem priors would face), so the natural implementation widens `ConstraintKind` to `"required" | "prohibited" | "prior"`. The moment that happens, `RosterModal.tsx:94`'s `if (p.kind === "required") cons.require(p.a,p.b); else cons.prohibit(p.a,p.b);` silently calls `cons.prohibit` on every prior pair — a soft 'please stay buddies' preference compiles and runs as a hard 'never be buddies' ban in the pre-generate feasibility check. `constraints.ts:57`'s `(p.kind === "required" ? required : prohibited).push(...)` does the same in the wire payload sent to the worker.
remediation: Before F9 lands, convert both branch sites to an exhaustive switch with an assertNever default (matching the pattern already established in GraphCanvas.tsx and highlight.ts), so adding "prior" to ConstraintKind fails to compile at every consumer until handled, instead of silently landing in the `prohibited` bucket.
invariant: for every function that branches on ConstraintPair.kind, adding a new ConstraintKind variant must fail to compile at that function until a case is added — no if/else or ternary may treat an unhandled variant as the same-shaped `else` branch.

theme: incomplete messaging masks multiple distinct failure modes, risking silent divergence when similar logic is extended
summary: Message 'don't match anyone in this roster' misleads when rules are dropped due to deduplication or self-pairing, not just missing names.
failure: User creates duplicate rules (Alice+Bob, Alice+Bob) or self-pair rules (Alice+Alice). One is dropped and counted in `resolved.dropped`. Message displays as "X buddy rules don't match anyone" — misleading, because the problem is duplication/self-pairing, not missing names.
remediation: Split `resolveNamedPairs` to return separate counts for drops by reason (missing_names, self_pairs, duplicates) OR change message to 'don't match anyone or are duplicates/invalid in this roster' to honestly describe all cases. Trace through the drop scenarios to name the theme once, so a later extension doesn't break the message without noticing.
invariant: When resolveNamedPairs returns dropped > 0, the user message must accurately describe every reason a rule was dropped (missing roster name, self-pair, or duplicate kind/pair), not just the first one.

theme: the roster dialog claims to be modal but nothing in the app actually confines keyboard focus to it or hides the background from the accessibility tree
summary: RosterModal (app/src/panels/RosterModal.tsx:106, role="dialog" aria-modal="true") is rendered as a sibling AFTER the entire background view (App.tsx:184-241) inside the same <main>, with no focus trap, no initial focus placement, and no `inert`/`aria-hidden` applied to the background while it is open. `aria-modal="true"` is a claim, not an enforcement mechanism — nothing in the codebase implements the trap (grep of app/src for .focus()/autoFocus/inert/aria-hidden returns nothing relevant).
failure: Cold load -> paste roster -> Generate (modal closes, view renders) -> click 'Edit people' (App.tsx:206) to reopen the dialog over the existing graph. A keyboard user now pressing Tab from the top of the page (or a screen-reader user doing a fresh linear read) walks through every background control — #rail's reroll/edit buttons, the layout toggle, the search combobox, PersonPanel/PathPanel if open, the entire buddy list, and the quality panel's Import/Print/Export buttons — before ever reaching a single control inside the 'modal' dialog that is visually covering the whole screen (app.css:180, z-index:20, inset:0, background blur). Shift+Tab from the dialog's first control also escapes into that same background rather than wrapping.
remediation: Give the dialog a real focus trap (a `useFocusTrap`-style effect that cycles Tab/Shift+Tab among the dialog's own focusable elements) and move initial focus into the dialog (e.g. the textarea) on mount; apply `inert` (or a manual aria-hidden + disabled sweep) to the sibling background content for the duration modalOpen is true.

theme: no component in the app ever restores focus after removing the element that currently holds it, so several ordinary interactions silently strand keyboard/screen-reader focus at document.body
summary: Every place a currently-focused control's own click handler causes that control to be removed from the DOM leaves focus nowhere: (1) PersonPanel's Close button (PersonPanel.tsx:59) calls onClose -> setSelected(null), unmounting the whole `#person` section (App.tsx:214-225); (2) PathPanel's Clear button (PathPanel.tsx:29) calls onClear -> path.clear(), unmounting `#route` (App.tsx:227-236); (3) RosterModal's Generate/Cancel buttons (RosterModal.tsx:151-158) unmount the entire dialog (App.tsx:243, 116/251); (4) the busy overlay's Cancel button (App.tsx:259) calls cancelGeneration, unmounting `.busy` (App.tsx:255-262). In every case there is no `.focus()` call anywhere in app/src to re-target focus, so per standard DOM behavior the browser drops focus to <body> when the focused element is detached.
failure: Select a person, open their PersonPanel, press Enter/Space on 'Close' (focused) — the panel disappears and focus is now on <body>; the next Tab press starts over from the top of the document instead of continuing from a sensible point (e.g. back to the buddy-list row that was open, or to search). Same for clearing a drawn path, and for closing the roster dialog via Cancel/Generate after edits.
remediation: On each of these unmounts, programmatically move focus to a specific, still-mounted element: e.g. Close/Back -> the BuddyList row for the closed person or the search input; PathPanel Clear -> the PersonPanel/search that started the route; dialog Cancel/Generate -> the '#rail' 'Edit people' button that opened it (or the app root on first generation); busy-overlay Cancel -> the control that started generation.

theme: an aria-live region only announces reliably if it already exists before its text is written; several regions in this app are mounted and populated in the same render, which is the exact anti-pattern Notice.tsx documents and avoids for its own toast, but the newer F10 path UI repeats it
summary:
`

` (PathPanel.tsx:33, :39, :45) is never present in the DOM until the state it describes already exists: PathPanel itself is only mounted when `path.active` becomes true (App.tsx:227, `{path.active && }`), and it starts with `from` already set (usePathFinder.start sets state synchronously before the next render). So the very first paint of 'Starting from X — now pick the other person' is a brand-new DOM node with text already inside it, not a mutation of a pre-existing live region — which many screen readers do not announce. The same happens again when `from` flips to `route`/`unreachable`: the 'from' paragraph unmounts and a *different* paragraph mounts fresh with the route/unreachable text, rather than one stable region having its text content updated. Notice.tsx's own comment (lines 9-11) states the correct pattern ("the region stays mounted even with no message... unmounting and remounting it with text is announced far less reliably") — PathPanel does the thing Notice explicitly avoids.
failure: Open PersonPanel for a person, press 'Find a path from here' (PersonPanel.tsx:87) — a screen-reader user gets no reliable announcement that a path pick is now pending, and must discover it by manually navigating to `#route`. Completing the route (selecting the second person) has the same gap for 'No chain — they're in separate groups' and the resulting chain text.
remediation:
Render `#route`'s live-region paragraph unconditionally (always mounted, initially empty like Notice's toast-region) and update its text content in place across from/route/unreachable transitions instead of conditionally mounting three different

elements.

theme: a UI state transition that is only conveyed by content appearing in the DOM, with no live region and no focus move, is invisible to a non-visual user
summary:
The zero-match state (`matches.length === 0`, PersonSearch.tsx:112-114, rendering `
Nobody matches "{query}"
`) sits inside `role="listbox"` (line 95) but nothing about it is exposed to assistive tech: the input's `aria-activedescendant` is `undefined` when there are no matches (line 78, since `activeIndex` is -1), the listbox itself has no `aria-live`, and ArrowUp/ArrowDown are no-ops when `matches.length === 0` (onKeyDown, lines 43-45), so there is no way to arrow into the empty message either. A sighted user sees the text; a screen-reader user typing the same query hears nothing at all.
failure: Type a misspelled name into 'Find a person' (e.g. cold-load a roster, then search for a name with a typo) — the combobox stays silently open with zero perceivable feedback via a screen reader; there is no way to tell the difference between 'still loading', 'nothing typed registered', and 'no one matches'.
remediation: Add a visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` status node (present at mount, alongside or inside the search widget) that is updated with 'No matches' text when `matches.length === 0`, independent of the visual `search-empty` div and independent of `aria-activedescendant`.

theme: a state that has a live-region pattern used correctly elsewhere in this app (Notice.tsx) is not given one at all for generation-in-progress, so the one visual indicator that anything is happening has no non-visual counterpart
summary:
The `.busy` overlay (App.tsx:255-262, `{bg.status === "running" &&
...Generating…...`) has no `role="status"`/`aria-live` anywhere, unlike Notice.tsx which deliberately keeps its `role="status"` region always-mounted for exactly this reason. Generation is asynchronous (runs in a Web Worker per app/CLAUDE.md) and can take a non-trivial time at larger roster sizes; there is currently zero accessible signal that a run started, is in progress, or (short of an eventual error toast or the graph silently swapping) that it's still going.
failure: Paste a large roster and press 'Generate buddy graph', or press 'Different arrangement' on an existing graph — a screen-reader user gets no announcement that generation began, and if it takes any perceptible time has no way to know the app is working versus stuck.
remediation: Give the busy overlay's text node role="status" (or route the 'Generating…'/done transition through the same always-mounted status-region pattern Notice.tsx already established).

theme: DOM/tab order for the absolutely-positioned panels does not track their on-screen spatial position, and the two panels M3 added make the existing zigzag worse
summary: All side panels are `position: absolute` (app.css: #search bottom-left, #person top-right, #route bottom-left, #buddies top-right, #metrics bottom bar) but DOM/tab order follows App.tsx's JSX order: search (bottom-left) -> person (top-right) -> route (bottom-left) -> buddies (top-right) -> metrics (bottom). A sequential Tab traversal bounces bottom-left/top-right/bottom-left/top-right before reaching the bottom bar, rather than following any consistent reading order (e.g. top-to-bottom, left-to-right).
failure: With a person selected and a path active, Tab from the search box lands on the top-right PersonPanel, then back down-left to PathPanel, then back up-right to BuddyList — a keyboard user has to track focus across the screen in a pattern that doesn't match how a sighted user would scan it.
remediation: Reorder the JSX (or use CSS order/flex reordering deliberately, keeping DOM order matching intended reading order) so panels in the same visual column/quadrant are adjacent in tab order; at minimum group #person and #buddies (both top-right) and #search/#route (both bottom-left) consecutively.

theme: the one plain-language constraint-outcome sentence is gated on the user-authored rule count, which structurally cannot include F9's auto-derived priors, so the flagship report ('kept 46 of 50 pairs') would render nothing in the common case
summary: constraintSummary(view) returns null whenever view.constraints.length === 0, but F9's priors are derived from the previous graph's edges each regenerate (not a user-authored ConstraintPair), so a preserve-only regenerate with no manually-added required/prohibited rules — the common F9 case, e.g. 'Dave joins, nobody has typed any buddy rules' — would hit the early return and silently show nothing, even though view.report.priorsKeptFraction (already plumbed opaquely through GraphView.report from the core's ConstraintReport) is populated.
failure:
Generate a graph with zero required/prohibited rules and priorWeight-driven priors; report.priorsKeptFraction is a real fraction (e.g. 0.92) but constraintSummary(view) returns null at the total===0 guard, so QualityPanel's `{rules &&
{rules}
}` renders nothing — F9's acceptance criterion ('report shows kept N of M pairs') is unmet for the case the feature exists for.
remediation: Give priors-kept a summary path independent of view.constraints.length — either fold report.priorsKeptFraction into constraintSummary's gate condition (`total===0 && report?.priorsKeptFraction==null`) or add a sibling summary function/render line in QualityPanel, so the two concerns (rule satisfaction vs. churn preservation) stay the same kind of always-checked-together the file's own comments already argue for with connectionSummary vs constraintSummary.
invariant: whenever view.report?.priorsKeptFraction is non-null, some rendered UI string reflects it — never gated behind view.constraints.length > 0, since priors and named rules are populated independently.

theme: the app's roster/settings/rules state describes the last ATTEMPTED generation rather than the graph currently on screen, so a button that promises to re-arrange THIS roster can silently swap in a different one
summary: handleGenerate commits `names`/`settings`/`constraints` at DISPATCH time (lines 118-125), but the displayed `view` is only replaced when the worker result arrives. Cancel (`cancelGeneration`, line 149 — keeps the old view) and the error path (line 99-104 — reopens the modal only when there is no view) both leave those three states describing a roster that was never generated. `handleReroll` then reads `names`/`settings`/`constraints` instead of `view.names`/`view.settings`/`view.constraints`, so "↻ Different arrangement" regenerates the abandoned roster — and its feasibility/rerollBlockReason preflight is also computed against the wrong n. The existing suite does not cover it (249 tests pass with the bug present); appErrorRecovery.test.tsx exercises the error/refusal toasts but never a reroll afterwards.
failure: Reproduced with a React harness driving the real App with a stubbed generation worker: generate roster A (5 people) → success, rail shows "5". Click "Edit people", type a 9-name roster, Generate, then either click Cancel in the busy overlay or let the worker report an error (no modal reopens because a view exists). Rail still shows "5". Now click "↻ Different arrangement": the dispatched request is {n:9,k:4}, not {n:5,k:4}, and when it returns the on-screen graph is replaced by the 9-person roster — from a control whose only stated effect is a different arrangement of the graph you are looking at. The refusal path is the same shape (names/constraints already switched to the refused input while graph A is displayed).
remediation: Make the displayed view the single source for regeneration: `handleReroll` should build its request from `view.names`, `view.settings` and `view.constraints` (feasibility and rerollBlockReason included), or commit `names`/`settings`/`constraints` only when a result is adopted (i.e. derive them from `view` and keep the in-flight inputs in the pending ref that useBuddyGraph already owns). Add a regression test: after a cancelled/errored second generation, the next reroll must dispatch n === view.names.length.
invariant: For every regeneration dispatched by the reroll control, the request's (n, k, constraints) equal (view.names.length, view.settings.buddies, view.constraints) of the view rendered at click time — a reroll can never change the roster identity of the displayed graph.

theme: a flat n threshold stands in for the core's real auto-polish decision, so the UI asserts a re-roll is impossible for rosters where the core would in fact vary the graph
summary: POLISH_MAX_N is a flat 120 and `rerollBlockReason` blocks every reroll above it with "This group is too large to shuffle — a different arrangement is only possible for smaller groups." But the core's auto-polish gate is no longer an n<=120 literal: `resolveWantPolish` compares `polishWork(n,k,defaultIters)` to MAX_POLISH_WORK, which is calibrated to reproduce 120 only at k=4. The real cutoff is k-dependent (unconstrained: 146 at k=2, 131 at k=3, 120 at k=4, 78 at k=12) and different again for the constrained builder (124-232, and MAX_CONSTRAINED_N=5000 so those sizes are all reachable in-app). Above 120 with k<4 the app therefore refuses to even dispatch, while the core would polish and the seed would change the graph. app/test/reroll.test.ts pins the boundary at k=4 only, so the whole k!=4 band is untested and the suite stays green.
failure: Direct core probe (lib/dist, default polish iterations): buildBuddyGraph(125, 3, {seed:1}) vs {seed:2} → polished=true, edges DIFFER, aspl 4.711 vs 4.719. Also polished=true at n=131/140/146 for k=2-3, and false at n=121 for k=4. In the app, a 125-person roster with "Buddies each" = 3 clicking "↻ Different arrangement" gets the flash "This group is too large to shuffle — a different arrangement is only possible for smaller groups." and no request is ever sent — a false impossibility claim that also removes the feature for that band. (The same constant drives useBuddyGraph's polish:true→"auto" downgrade at line 121, which is harmless in the direction tested but rests on the same wrong predicate.)
remediation: Take it lib-first: export the core's own auto-polish predicate (e.g. `autoPolishes(n, k, { constrained })` wrapping resolveWantPolish/polishWork) and have `rerollBlockReason` and the polish downgrade call it, deleting the flat POLISH_MAX_N. Then parameterize app/test/reroll.test.ts over k (not just k=4) so the app's block can never claim impossibility where the core polishes.
invariant: For all n and settings, if rerollBlockReason(n, settings) returns the too-large reason then the core would not polish that configuration — i.e. buildBuddyGraph(n, settings.buddies, {polish: settings.polish, polishIters: 1}).polished === false (and the constrained equivalent when constraints are in force).

theme: a small imported file materializes hundreds of megabytes of synchronous text on the main thread, because nothing bounds a single name's length or a single person's degree — only their aggregates
summary: importGraph's two size gates bound only AVERAGES, so the product (degree of one person) x (length of one name) is unbounded. The density gate is `2 * f.edges.length > BUDDY_MAX * f.people.length` — average degree — so a star graph with one hub of degree n-1 (999 at n=1000) passes trivially (2*999 <= 12*1000). The name gate is `joined.length > MAX_PARSE_CHARS` — total roster characters — so a single name may be ~500,000 chars. Neither gate exists per-vertex or per-name. The hub's 480,000-char name is then the buddy label of all 999 leaves, and `buddyLabel` is called once per person by BuddyList (visible), Slips (always mounted, aria-hidden), and toCsv. Note `app/src/neighborhood.ts:10` explicitly documents the assumption "Degree is capped at BUDDY_MAX = 12", which is false on the import path.
failure: A 512,696-byte JSON file (well under readFileText's 8 MB gate) — version 1, people[0].name = "x".repeat(480000), people[1..999] = "p1".."p999", edges = [[0,1]..[0,999]] — is ACCEPTED by importGraph in 125 ms. Reproduced in .review-scratch/hub.probe.test.ts: the accepted view yields degreeMax 999 and Sum over i of buddyLabel(view,i).length = 479,525,884 characters. BuddyList and Slips each render that as DOM text on one synchronous React commit (~480 MB per subtree, ~960 MB across both); node RSS reached 1,065 MB. Pressing CSV builds a 480,015,788-character string (2.6 s in node, before Blob/download). This is a tab freeze/OOM from a half-megabyte file.
remediation: Add a per-name length cap (e.g. `export const MAX_NAME_CHARS`) enforced in BOTH authorities — parseRoster (truncate or drop with a warning, so the round-trip check stays consistent) and importGraph (refuse: "A name is too long") — and add a per-vertex degree gate to importGraph alongside the existing density gate: after the edge loop, refuse when `degreeExtent(g.degrees())[1] > BUDDY_MAX` ("someone has N buddies — more than a buddy graph allows"). Both checks must run before `allPairsSummary`/view construction. Update neighborhood.ts's degree-cap note once (b) is real.
invariant: For EVERY GraphView the app accepts (import or generate), the total text its buddy-label sinks (BuddyList, Slips, toCsv, clipboard copy) materialize is bounded by a file-independent constant: Sum over i<n of (names[i].length + buddyLabel(view,i).length) <= MAX_ROSTER_N * (BUDDY_MAX + 2) * MAX_NAME_CHARS. Enforceable as two per-element gates that must hold for every accepted file: (a) every name satisfies names[i].length <= MAX_NAME_CHARS, and (b) max over v of degree(v) <= BUDDY_MAX. Any accepted input violating the aggregate bound is a failure.

theme: raw content from an untrusted file is echoed verbatim and unbounded into the on-screen error toast
summary: ImportError messages interpolate untrusted file values with no length bound, and App's catch renders them straight into the DOM: `flash(\`Couldn't import that file: ${err.message}\`)` (App.tsx:176) -> useNotice state -> `<button className="toast">{message}</button>` (Notice.tsx:23) — a single text node in a styled, wrapping toast. Two reachable sites: `Unsupported file version: ${JSON.stringify(f.version)}` (importGraph.ts:137) and `Person "${p.name}" has id ${p.id}...` (importGraph.ts:168, which fires BEFORE the joined-length check at line 190, so the name is unbounded there). Nothing between the throw and the text node truncates. The whole file-byte budget (8 MB) is therefore convertible into one DOM text node, and the toast stays mounted for AUTO_CLEAR_MS = 4000 before a second layout pass removes it.
failure: Reproduced in .review-scratch/echo.probe.test.ts: `{"version":"AAAA..."}` with a 7,900,000-character version string is 7,900,014 bytes — under readFileText's 8,000,000-byte gate — JSON.parses fine, and importGraph throws an ImportError whose `.message` is 7,900,042 characters. App's handler makes that a 7,900,069-character toast string handed to React as the sole child of the toast button. The id-mismatch path is equally unbounded: a 7,000,000-char `name` yields a 7,000,040-char message. Message length is measured; the resulting multi-second glyph-shaping/line-breaking block is inferred from the character count, not measured in a browser.
remediation: Add one truncating quoter used at every interpolation of untrusted file content (e.g. `function quote(v: unknown, max = 80)` returning `JSON.stringify(v).slice(0, max)` plus an ellipsis) and apply it at importGraph.ts:137 and :168. Belt-and-braces: clamp in the single sink instead of/as well as at each site — truncate to NOTICE_MAX_CHARS inside `useNotice`'s `show`/`flash` (app/src/state/useNotice.ts), which bounds every present and future message producer rather than only the two known ones.
invariant: Every string that reaches the Notice sink — i.e. every argument passed to useNotice's `show`/`flash`, including every `ImportError.message` — has length <= NOTICE_MAX_CHARS, a constant independent of the imported file's content. Equivalently: no untrusted value is interpolated into a user-facing message without first passing through a truncating quoter.

theme: the app's structured pre-check (used to get a named, per-person refusal instead of the lib's prose) validates a different constraint set than the lib actually builds against, and the two are not kept in sync by any shared code path
summary: runGeneration's existing pattern for F7 (validate a raw Constraints up front so refusals can be structured Reason[] instead of prose, then trust buildConstrainedBuddyGraph to succeed) does not compose with F9/priorHard. buildConstrainedBuddyGraph internally promotes priors to required BEFORE validating (lib/src/core/index.ts:308, withHardPriors), but the app's pre-check at generate.ts:97 (validateDetailed(cons, k)) would run against the UN-promoted set if a straightforward F9 patch just adds cons.addPrior(...) + cons.priorHard = true to the same Constraints object the app already builds (mirroring how required/prohibited are added at lines 94-95). generate.ts's own comment at line 76-79 already flags this exact gap: '...checking first is what lets the refusal carry structured reasons... identical here, since the app has no priors to promote' — i.e. the code already knows this equivalence breaks the day priors exist, and nothing currently enforces re-deriving the pre-check from the same promotion path the builder uses.
failure: Reproduced directly against lib/dist: n=4, k=2, cons.addPrior(0,1), addPrior(0,2), addPrior(0,3), cons.priorHard=true. validateDetailed(cons, k) on the unpromoted object returns [] (feasible) — this is what a naive F9 pre-check, following the existing required/prohibited pattern, would report. But buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(4, 2, cons, {}) internally promotes priors to required first and correctly refuses: report.refusals = ['person 0 has 3 required buddies but each person gets 2'], edges = [], buddies = [[],[],[],[]]. generate.ts's fromConstrained (line 48) packages this unconditionally as kind: 'ok' (runGeneration line 100) with no check of r.report.refusals.length — so the UI would render a graph where everyone has zero buddies, with no 'refused' overlay, no reopened editor, no named-person explanation — the exact silent-partial F7's acceptance criteria (PROJECT_PLAN.md:101, 'never a silent partial') were written to forbid, reintroduced by F9 through a channel F7 already closed for required/prohibited.
remediation: When adding priors/priorHard, run the app's pre-check against the SAME promoted constraint set the builder will use — e.g. expose/call the promotion step (or just always run priors through cons.require(a,b) locally before validateDetailed when priorHard is set, mirroring withHardPriors) rather than validating the raw object. Alternatively, have runGeneration check result.report.refusals.length > 0 after calling buildConstrainedBuddyGraph and return a refused-shaped response (even if only with prose, since the builder's refusal path doesn't carry structured Reason[]) instead of trusting the pre-check to have already caught every case.
invariant: For every Constraints cons and buddy count k the app hands to the worker: validateDetailed(cons_as_the_app_pre-checks_it, k).length === 0 must imply buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(n, k, cons, opts).report.refusals.length === 0. Currently false whenever cons.priorHard === true and promoting priors to required pushes some person's required-degree, or a required/prohibited conflict, past what k/prohibited pairs allow.

theme: the worker protocol and constraint editor have no representation for priors/priorHard at all yet
summary: GenerateRequest.constraints only carries {required, prohibited} (protocol.ts:22-25) and GenerateOptions has no priorWeight/priorHard (protocol.ts:4-8); ConstraintPair/ConstraintKind (constraints.ts:12-23) has no 'prior' concept and priors aren't user-authored named rules anyway (they'd need to be derived from the PREVIOUS view's edges, resolved by name against the possibly-changed roster — there is no existing helper analogous to resolveNamedPairs for a plain edge list). None of this has a caller today; per the no-caller rule this is filed as a deferral, not a blocking gap — it's necessary groundwork for F9 but building it before F9 is designed (in particular before deciding where the 'preserve current buddies' toggle lives — RosterModal is the natural 'Edit people' surface but doesn't currently receive the live view's edges) would be exactly the anti-pattern app/CLAUDE.md already warns against (extension seam for an unbuilt feature).

theme: Constraint object building duplicated in two code paths with different input orderings
summary: The logic to build a Constraints object from a set of pairs is duplicated in two locations that process constraints in different orders. The main thread (RosterModal) processes require/prohibit calls in the order the user edited them (potentially intermixed), while the worker (generate.ts) processes all required pairs first, then all prohibited pairs. This creates a latent maintenance hazard despite current order-independence.
failure: Hypothetical: If the Constraints class implementation were optimized to depend on call order (e.g., early exit or greedy assignment based on prior choices), the main thread validation could report a rule set as feasible while the worker generates a refusal—a silent discrepancy. More immediately, a refactor that extracts a helper function in one location but forgets to update the other would diverge the implementations.
remediation: Extract the constraint-building logic into a shared function that takes a ConstraintPair[] and preserves the normalized order (all required, then all prohibited) consistently across both paths. This ensures future maintainers can't accidentally diverge the implementations, and it documents the expected calling order explicitly. The function would live in constraints.ts, pair with resolveNamedPairs and splitPairs.
invariant: For any set of buddy rules, the feasibility validation performed on the main thread (RosterModal, line 97) must produce identical results to the feasibility check performed in the worker (generate.ts, line 97), regardless of whether the constraints are added to a Constraints object in user-edit order or in separated required/prohibited order.

theme: the focus trap meant to keep keyboard/AT users OUT of the app behind the dialog instead makes the dialog itself unreachable, because it nests the dialog inside the very subtree it marks inert
summary: RosterModal (the roster-setup dialog, role="dialog" aria-modal="true") is rendered INSIDE <div id="app" inert={modalOpen}> (inside <main>, lines 255-265), not as a sibling as the adjacent comment (lines 182-185) claims. `inert` cascades to all descendants per the HTML spec and browser implementations, with no way for a nested element to opt back in. So the moment modalOpen is true — including on cold load, since `modalOpen` is initialised to `true` (line 44) — div#app AND everything inside it, including RosterModal itself, is inert: removed from the accessibility tree and unfocusable/untabbable. A screen-reader-and-keyboard-only user gets a page that announces essentially nothing operable on first paint (no textarea, no Generate button reachable), and re-opening the modal later via "Edit people" has the same effect.
failure: Cold load with a screen reader and no mouse: press Tab. Because #app (containing #modal) is inert, the roster textarea, "choose a file"/"try example names" links, the buddy-rules editor, settings controls, and "Generate buddy graph" button are all outside the accessibility tree and outside the tab order — Tab lands nowhere useful, and the dialog that is the ONLY thing on screen cannot be operated without a mouse. Verified structurally and with a jsdom render (`appDiv.hasAttribute('inert') === true` and `appDiv.contains(modalDiv) === true` both hold) in a scratch test at app/test/__scratch_inert.test.tsx (run then removed).
remediation: Render RosterModal as an actual sibling of the inert div, outside `<div id="app" inert={modalOpen}>` — e.g. move the `{modalOpen && <RosterModal .../>}` block (and ideally the busy overlay too, for the same reason) to sit alongside `<div id="app">` in the top-level fragment, matching what the comment already says is the design.
invariant: Whenever an element carrying `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"` is open, that element and its descendants must never be a descendant of any element carrying the `inert` attribute (equivalently: `inertAncestor.contains(dialogElement)` must be false for every element with `inert` truthy).

theme: closing/replacing a panel unmounts the very element that had focus with no explicit refocus, so the browser drops focus to <body> and a keyboard/screen-reader user loses their place in the document
summary: PersonPanel's "Close" button (`onClick={onClose}` -> `setSelected(null)` in App.tsx) and PathPanel's "Clear" button (`onClick={onClear}` -> `path.clear()`) both cause the panel — and the very button that was just activated — to unmount entirely (`{selected !== null && <PersonPanel .../>}` / `{path.active && <PathPanel .../>}` in App.tsx). Neither App.tsx nor any hook in the app (`useEscape`, `useExplorerHistory`, `usePathFinder`) ever calls `.focus()` on a replacement target — a whole-tree grep for `.focus(`, `autoFocus`, `activeElement` across app/src found zero occurrences outside GraphCanvas's own selection highlighting. When a focused element is removed from the DOM, focus moves to `<body>` (spec-defined), so the next Tab press restarts tab order from the top of the document instead of continuing near where the user was working. The same applies to Escape-driven clears (`useEscape` calling `path.clear()`/`explorer.select(null)`), which remove PathPanel/PersonPanel the same way.
failure: Keyboard/screen-reader session: select a person (PersonPanel appears, focus e.g. on "Find a path from here"), start a path, then press the PathPanel's "Clear" button. PathPanel unmounts; focus is now on <body>. The next Tab press jumps to the header/brand area at the top of the page rather than back to PersonPanel or anything related to the person just being explored — the user has to re-navigate the whole page to resume.
remediation: On any control whose activation removes its own containing panel (Close, Clear, Cancel-generation-that-reopens-modal, etc.), explicitly move focus to a stable anchor before/after the unmount — e.g. a ref on the triggering panel's sibling control ("Edit people", the search input, or the row in BuddyList that opened PersonPanel) — rather than relying on default browser behavior.
invariant: For every control whose activation causes its own ancestor panel to unmount, `document.activeElement` immediately after the state update must be a specific, still-mounted, previously-identified element — never `document.body`.
