theme: a result that carries "no graph was produced" can reach the view as a normal success and render as satisfied rules
summary: `runGeneration` maps whatever `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph` returns into kind:"ok" without inspecting `report.refusals`. That builder REFUSES rather than throws (lib/src/core/index.ts:289-310, refusedResult at 464): it returns n empty buddy lists, zero edges, aspl/diameter 0, connected:false, largestComponentFraction:0, satisfied:false, reqViolations:0, prohViolations:0, refusals:[...]. Fed through viewFromResult/assembleMetrics that becomes a view whose `constraintSummary` prints "all N buddy rules satisfied" (it tests reqViolations+prohViolations===0 and never looks at satisfied/refusals) over a graph with no edges. Today the app's own `validateDetailed` pre-check makes the builder's refusal branches unreachable (cons.n === n by construction, n <= 1000 << MAX_ROSTER), which is why this is PLAUSIBLE rather than reproduced — but the ok channel is the wrong place to discover that assumption broke, and the failure mode is the exact disconnected-reads-as-optimal class this app guards elsewhere.
failure: If any builder refusal path is ever reachable (a new refusal reason in `validate` that `validateDetailed` gates differently, a future priors/tags path, or a caller of runGeneration that skips the pre-check), the response is kind:"ok" and the UI shows an edgeless graph with the rules line "all 3 buddy rules satisfied" and a 0% gauge, instead of the refusal toast that names the people involved.
remediation: In `fromConstrained`/`runGeneration`, treat a non-empty `r.report.refusals` as the refusal channel (return kind:"refused", mapping the reasons, or kind:"error" if only prose is available), and/or have `constraintSummary` refuse to print "satisfied" for a report whose `satisfied` is false with zero violations. Cover it with a unit test on runGeneration's mapping.
invariant: runGeneration never returns kind:"ok" for a result whose report.refusals is non-empty; and no GraphView with zero edges and n>1 ever renders a rules line asserting satisfaction.

theme: a number the panel prints disagrees with the metric the core measured, in the direction that makes a broken graph look emptier/better than it is
summary: connectionSummary floors the largest-group share, so a badly shattered graph is reported as "0% are in the largest group" even though the largest group is non-empty — the guard exists at the top of the range (Math.min(99, …)) but not at the bottom.
failure: importGraph({version:1, people:[101 people], edges:[]}) → metrics.largestComponentFraction = 0.00990… and connectionSummary prints "not everyone's connected — 0% are in the largest group". Same for 302 people with a single edge (fraction 0.0066 → "0%"). Reproduced in .review-scratch/cr3/frac.probe.ts. The existing suite pins the 99 ceiling (app/test/quality.test.ts:46) and nothing pins the floor, so this passes today.
remediation: Clamp the displayed percentage into [1, 99] whenever the graph is disconnected and largestComponentFraction > 0 — the same one-line symmetry the existing Math.min(99, …) guard already applies at the other end (e.g. Math.max(1, Math.min(99, Math.floor(f*100)))). Fix it in connectionSummary, the single caption seam, so no sibling sink can re-derive it.
invariant: For every Metrics m produced by assembleMetrics with m.connected === false, the integer percentage rendered by connectionSummary(m) is 0 if and only if m.largestComponentFraction === 0; otherwise it lies in [1, 99].

theme: a buddy rule the user authored disappears without being told it was deleted — the silent-partial the constraints feature exists to prevent
summary: On Generate the modal hands App only `resolved.pairs`, so any rule row that named someone not in the roster (or a self-pair, or a duplicate) is permanently discarded; the app's stored rule model is index pairs, so reopening "Edit people" cannot show it again — contradicting the editor's own stated contract that an unrecognised row is "kept and flagged rather than deleted".
failure: Open the roster modal with roster [Alice…Fran]; add rule (Alice, Zoe) — the note says "1 buddy rule names someone who isn't in this roster and won't be used" (present tense, not "will be discarded") — add a valid rule (Ben, Chloe); click Generate; reopen the modal seeded exactly as App seeds it (constraints=stored pairs, constraintNames=stored names). Two rows in, one row out. Reproduced in .review-scratch/cr3/rules.jprobe.tsx: expected 2 rule rows, got 1. The sibling is the roster-edit cycle the NamedPair design was built for: remove Dev from the roster text, Generate, re-add Dev — every Dev rule is gone for good, because App never held the name form. Existing tests (app/test/constraintsFlow.test.tsx) assert only that the unmatched pair is absent from onGenerate's payload, so the loss on reopen is unasserted.
remediation: Make the NAME-keyed list the model App stores (App keeps NamedPair[] and resolves to ConstraintPair[] only at dispatch, next to the roster in force), so the editor round-trips exactly what the user typed; resolution stays where it already is in `resolveNamedPairs`. This is subtraction — one conversion at the dispatch boundary instead of a conversion in and a lossy conversion out — and it closes the roster-edit sibling at the same time. If the rules really are meant to be dropped, the note must say so ("…and will be removed") rather than "won't be used".
invariant: For every editor state, the multiset of rule rows rendered after (Generate → reopen the roster modal) equals the multiset of rule rows the editor held at Generate; no row is removed without a message that states the row was removed.

theme: the guard that bounds untrusted file content in an error message does its bounding after the expensive step, so the guard itself becomes the failure
summary: `quote()` serializes the entire untrusted value with `JSON.stringify` and only then slices to 80 chars, so a deeply-nested value throws a RangeError that escapes `importGraph` as a non-ImportError, and a multi-megabyte value costs a full serialization to produce 80 characters.
failure: Import a file `{"version": X}` where X is a 20,000-deep nested array (JSON.parse handles 200,000 deep in 83 ms, so this parses fine). `quote(f.version)` at line 151 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` instead of an `ImportError`; App.handleImportFile catches it as a generic Error and the toast reads "Couldn't import that file: Maximum call stack size exceeded" — an engine-internal string in a module whose entire contract is plain-language refusal. Same leak via `quote(p.id)` at line 193 with `{"version":1,"people":[{"id":<nested 20000>,"name":"a"},{"name":"b"}],"edges":[[0,1]]}`. Cost variant, same root cause: `{"version":"A".repeat(7_000_000)}` refuses correctly but takes 60 ms and allocates the whole 7 MB serialization to keep 80 characters.
remediation: Bound the input before serializing rather than the output after. In `quote`, handle primitives only — for a string, slice to `max` BEFORE `JSON.stringify`; for a number/boolean/null, stringify directly; for anything else return a structural description (`"a list of 1000000 items"`, `"an object"`) without recursing. That closes both the RangeError and the O(|value|) allocation with one subtraction. Name the sibling: `quote` is called at two sites (`f.version`, `p.id`/`p.name`) and both are covered by fixing the helper, but the belt-and-braces half of the theme is that `importGraph` should be the single import authority — no caller should have to distinguish an `ImportError` from an engine error, so either wrap the body so only `ImportError` escapes, or have `App.handleImportFile` fall back to the generic message for a non-`ImportError`.
invariant: For every value `d` obtainable from `JSON.parse` of any string, `importGraph(d)` either returns a GraphView or throws an `ImportError` — no other error type ever escapes; and `quote(v)` returns within a constant bound of `max` for every `v`, never throwing.

theme: Function documentation describes only one return value when the function returns multiple distinct values that callers use for different error messages
summary: resolveNamedPairs comment says 'Returns the dropped count' but the function returns an object with five fields (pairs, unmatched, duplicate, selfPair, dropped)
failure: Developer reading the JSDoc comment for resolveNamedPairs learns only about 'dropped count' from the prose; the comment omits mention of unmatched, selfPair, and duplicate counts, which are all used by RosterModal to display distinct user-facing messages about different resolution failures (lines 170-190 of RosterModal.tsx)
remediation: Revise the comment starting at line 166 to document the full return object: 'Returns the resolved pairs and counts of resolution failures by cause (unmatched, self-pairs, duplicates) plus total dropped, so the caller can report each issue separately.' This matches the actual usage and return type signature.
invariant: Every exported function whose JSDoc describes a return value must document all fields in the actual return type. Specifically: the comment for resolveNamedPairs must mention that unmatched, duplicate, and selfPair are returned and are used by RosterModal for per-cause messages.

theme: App.tsx has a documented, tested focus-rescue mechanism (closeWithFocus) for the person/route panels, but the roster setup dialog and the busy overlay — which are ALSO removed-from-DOM-while-focused surfaces, closed by the user's own actions inside them — were never wired into it, so the exact bug the mechanism was built to prevent still happens through three other doors.
summary: Focus lands on document.body (stranding the next Tab back at the top of the page) after: (1) clicking 'Generate buddy graph' on cold load — the very first action in the scenario; (2) clicking 'Cancel' in the roster editor opened via 'Edit people' with an existing view; (3) clicking the busy overlay's 'Cancel' button while a re-roll is in progress. In every case the focused control (inside RosterModal or `.busy`) is unmounted by the state change its own onClick triggers (`setModalOpen(false)` in handleGenerate/onCancel, or the busy div disappearing when `bg.cancel()` returns status to 'done'), and nothing calls `.focus()` afterward the way `closeWithFocus` does for the person/route panels.
failure: Reproduced with RTL: render <App/>, type a roster, focus and click 'Generate buddy graph' -> document.activeElement === document.body. Same result focusing and clicking the editor's 'Cancel' with a view already present, and focusing/clicking the busy overlay's 'Cancel' during a reroll. A screen-reader/keyboard-only user in each case must now Tab from the very top of the document (past the header) to reach the graph that just appeared, instead of landing on the rail, search box, or wherever is contextually next — exactly the dead end App.tsx's own comment at line 73-76 describes and says 'nothing in the app called .focus() anywhere' to prevent, except three call sites of that same class were missed.
remediation: Route RosterModal's onGenerate/onCancel and the busy overlay's Cancel through the same closeWithFocus-style rescue used for the person/route panels — e.g. check `document.activeElement` before calling `setModalOpen(false)`/`bg.cancel()` and refocus `searchRef.current` (or, when no view exists yet and the modal reopens, a stable element inside the reopened modal) when the outgoing focus was inside the dialog or the busy overlay.
invariant: For every element E that is focused and then removed from the DOM as a direct result of activating E itself (RosterModal's Generate/Cancel buttons, the busy overlay's Cancel button, and the already-covered person/route panel close buttons), document.activeElement !== document.body immediately after the removal.

theme: A control's selected/current state is expressed only through a CSS class, with no ARIA counterpart, so a screen-reader user tabbing the list cannot tell which row is currently selected — the same class of gap LayoutToggle's aria-pressed and PersonSearch's aria-selected were added to close, just not extended to this list.
summary: The buddy-list row for the currently selected person gets a visible highlight (`.brow.sel { background: … }`, app.css:164) via `className={"brow" + (selected === i ? " sel" : "")}` (BuddyList.tsx:51), but the `<button>` carries no `aria-current` (or `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected`) reflecting that state, unlike LayoutToggle's `aria-pressed` for the identical 'which one of these is active' pattern.
failure: A screen-reader user who selects a person from the graph or search, then tabs through the buddy list to review it, gets no announcement distinguishing the selected row from any other — every row reads only as "<Name>: <buddies>, button", with no cue that one of them is the person currently shown in PersonPanel.
remediation: Add `aria-current={selected === i ? "true" : undefined}` (or `aria-pressed`) to the row button in BuddyList.tsx, mirroring LayoutToggle's pattern.
invariant: For every row whose selected/active state is expressed by a CSS class, the same button also carries an ARIA state attribute (aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-selected) that is true exactly when the class is applied.

theme: every other untrusted string in the app is capped at its sink; the search query is the one that is not
summary: The search query is stored, trimmed three times per render, and rendered in full into a DOM text node with no length cap — the only untrusted-string sink in the app without one (roster text is capped by `capText`, notices by `clampNotice`, names by `MAX_NAME_CHARS`).
failure: Paste several megabytes into the "Find a person…" box. `query` is held uncapped in state; `open` calls `query.trim()`, `rankMatches` calls `query.trim().toLowerCase()`, and the zero-match branch renders `Nobody matches “{query.trim()}”` — so each keystroke allocates ~3x the pasted size and hands the browser a multi-megabyte text node inside a small wrapping div. Marked PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED: I verified the code path and that `rankMatches` itself stays cheap (matchNormalized is bounded by the 120-char name cap regardless of query size), but I could not reproduce the browser layout cost under jsdom. NOT reachable from an imported file or roster — names are capped at 120 chars — so this is a self-inflicted paste only.
remediation: Cap at the sink the way `useNotice.clampNotice` already does: slice the query for display (and optionally add `maxLength` to the input), and trim once into a memo instead of three times per render. Subtraction, not a new guard.
invariant: No string rendered as DOM text by any component in app/src exceeds a declared per-sink character cap, for every input — including one that never passed through parseRoster or importGraph.

theme: Switch statement over discriminated union has no runtime guard against unhandled cases, relying only on compile-time test strictness
summary: describeReason function switches on Reason.code with no default case; if a new Reason code is added to ringweave and the test SAMPLES table is not updated, the app silently returns undefined
failure: A new Reason code added to the core's Reason type, if describeReason is not updated with a matching case, returns undefined implicitly. The test suite's Record<Reason['code'], Reason> type guard will catch the test failing to compile, but this only matters if the tests are run—runtime code could receive an unhandled code.
remediation: Add a default case to the switch statement that throws or logs an error: 'default: throw new Error(`Unhandled Reason code: ${r.code}`);' This makes failures explicit rather than silent, catching them immediately at runtime rather than relying on test-suite discipline.
invariant: describeReason(r, names) must always return a non-empty string for every possible Reason type. No input should result in undefined being returned or rendered.

theme: A transient success confirmation is expressed only as a change to the focused control's own visible text, with no accompanying live region — the same 'announcement, not just presence' gap Notice.tsx and PathPanel.tsx were explicitly built to avoid (see their comments about a live region needing to exist BEFORE the text change), just not extended to this control.
summary: `copyAll` (BuddyList.tsx:16-30) flips the Copy button's own label from "Copy" to "Copied" for 1100ms via `setCopied`, with no `aria-live`/`role="status"` region announcing the confirmation. A focused button's own accessible-name change is not reliably announced by screen readers the way a live region is — which is precisely the reasoning already applied to Notice.tsx (kept mounted so AT is 'already watching' it) and PathPanel.tsx (one live region, not three conditional ones).
failure: A screen-reader user who activates 'Copy' may hear nothing confirming the copy succeeded, and by the time they explore to find out, the 1100ms window may have already reverted the label back to "Copy" — indistinguishable from the click not having registered.
remediation: Add a small `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region (mounted permanently like Notice.tsx's toast-region) that receives "Copied" text on a successful copy, alongside (or instead of) the button-label swap.
invariant: caseOnly: could not state a fully machine-checkable invariant without simulating actual AT announcement behavior (button-label-change announcement reliability is a live-AT-implementation fact, not something a DOM assertion alone proves) — filed as a traced code-level gap (no live region exists for this confirmation) rather than a proven non-announcement.

theme: the connection score and its plain-language caption are measured against a yardstick that the graph's own (low) degree lowers, so a badly-connected group can read better than a well-connected one of the same size
summary: `assembleMetrics` scores quality against the graph's ACTUAL `degreeMax`, so a low-degree graph is judged against a low Moore bound; `connectionSummary`/`qualityPercent` then render that degree-relative gap as an absolute claim about the group, and the gauge and caption are non-monotone in the number of hops they sit next to.
failure:
Reproduced (`vite-node` against `app/src/model.ts` + `app/src/io/importGraph.ts`):
- Generation-reachable, no hand editing: `buildBuddyGraph(200, 2)` (buddies = BUDDY_MIN, n well under the cap) -> aspl 50.25, diameter 100, `qualityPercent` = **100**, `connectionSummary` = **"everyone's well-linked"**, `isOptimal` = true (so the reroll replies "That's already an optimal arrangement"). A 200-person daisy chain where the average pair is 50 hops apart is displayed as a perfect score.
- Import a 1000-person chain -> aspl 333.67, diameter 999, gauge **67**, caption **"everyone's well-linked"**.
- Import a 1000-person 12-regular circulant on the same n -> aspl 42.13, diameter 84, gauge **0**, caption "everyone's connected, but loosely linked".
The second graph is ~8x closer on every displayed distance than the first, on the same roster size, and scores 0 where the first scores 67. Existing tests (`app/test/quality.test.ts`) fix `Metrics` by hand and only pin the disconnected and rounding-boundary cases, so none of this fails the suite.
remediation: Close the theme where the yardstick is chosen, in `assembleMetrics`: stop letting the graph's own `degreeMax` move the bar. Score against a yardstick that is fixed for a given n (e.g. `mooreLowerBounds(n, BUDDY_MAX)`), or gate the plain-language tier in `connectionSummary` on an absolute distance criterion in addition to the gap. Do the same for `isOptimal`, which feeds the "a re-roll can't improve it" copy — that is the sibling one code path over, and fixing only the caption leaves it claiming perfection for a 200-person ring.
invariant: For all `n` and all `Metrics` A, B derived from graphs on that same `n` with `A.connected && B.connected`: `A.aspl > B.aspl` implies `qualityPercent(A) <= qualityPercent(B)` and the connection tier of A (split < loosely-linked < well-linked, as produced by `connectionSummary`) is not above the tier of B. The displayed score and caption must be monotone non-increasing in ASPL at fixed roster size.

theme: the path panel states a fact about the user's own action ("Starting from Dia") that the chain it then renders contradicts
summary: `usePathFinder` canonicalises the route on `min(from, to)` and returns it in that orientation, so when the user starts a path from the higher-indexed person the rendered chain reads from the OTHER end — directly contradicting the live-region sentence the same panel just announced.
failure: Reproduced with `renderHook(() => usePathFinder(g))` on a 6-ring with names [Ana, Ben, Chen, Dia, Eli, Fay]: `start(3)` makes `PathPanel` announce "Starting from **Dia** — now pick the other person."; `complete(0)` then yields `route = [0,1,2,3]`, which `PathPanel` renders as "Ana -> Ben -> Chen -> Dia". `expect(route[0]).toBe(3)` fails with `received 0`. The existing test `"draws the same line whichever end is picked first"` asserts the two orientations are `toEqual`, so it locks the defect in rather than catching it.
remediation: Keep the canonical computation (it is what makes s->t and t->s the same line), but orient the RESULT to the user's stated start: compute on `min/max` and reverse the array when `ends[0] !== route[0]`. A reversed shortest path is still a shortest path, so the drawn edge set is unchanged and the s<->t symmetry the canonicalisation exists for is preserved.
invariant: For all graphs and all `ends = [f, t]` with `f !== t`: if `route !== null` then `route[0] === f && route[route.length - 1] === t`, AND the route for `[f, t]` is exactly the reverse of the route for `[t, f]` (so the drawn chain is orientation-independent while the readout always starts where the user said it did).

theme: the generation worker has failure modes that never reach the UI, so a crash is indistinguishable from an in-progress run
summary: `attach` registers only `worker.onmessage`; nothing listens for the Worker's `error` or `messageerror` events, so a worker that fails to load or dies mid-run leaves `status === "running"` permanently — which keeps `#app` `inert` and the "Generating…" overlay up indefinitely.
failure: Reproduced under jsdom with a stubbed `Worker`: `renderHook(() => useGenerationWorker())`, `generate({n:5,k:2})` -> `status === "running"`; firing the worker's `onerror` leaves `status === "running"` (the probe logged that no handler was ever assigned). In `App`, `<div id="app" inert={modalOpen || bg.status === "running"}>` means the whole UI stays inert; only the Cancel button in the busy overlay recovers. This is not hypothetical for a Pages-deployed SPA: a stale/404'd worker chunk after a redeploy fires exactly this event. No test in `app/test/` covers it — `generateWorker.test.ts` tests `runGeneration` directly and `appErrorRecovery.test.tsx` mocks the hook away entirely.
remediation: Register `worker.onerror` and `worker.onmessageerror` alongside `onmessage` in `attach`, mapping both onto the existing `kind: "error"` state transition (clearing `runningRef`) so the already-tested `status === "error"` recovery path in `App` runs. That closes the theme rather than the single event: every way the worker can stop producing a response ends in a terminal status.
invariant: For all worker outcomes, `useGenerationWorker` must leave `status === "running"` only while a response for `latestId` is still possible: any terminal Worker event (`message`, `error`, `messageerror`) for the current id must transition `status` out of `"running"` and set `runningRef` false.

theme: untrusted names carrying invisible and control characters defeat the import guard and reach every name sink (DOM, print slips, CSV, clipboard)
summary: importGraph's control-character guard is a hand-written C0+DEL range (`/[�-]/`), not a Unicode category check, and parseRoster's normalizer (parseRoster.ts:34) has the identical range. The whole C1 control block (U+0080-U+009F, including NEL U+0085) and every Cf format character (U+00AD, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+206F, ...) pass both. They are not stripped by String.trim() either, so they also survive the parseRoster round-trip check at importGraph.ts:228 that is supposed to be the authority on which names are acceptable. Consequences reproduced from a file: (1) the round-trip check's own promise -- 'Every name must be non-empty, unique (case-insensitively)' -- is false, because zero-width characters make visually identical names distinct; (2) a name that is entirely invisible passes the non-empty check; (3) an unterminated bidi override reaches a shared DOM text node and reverses the rendering of everything after it; (4) 71 leading non-graphic code points sit in front of neutralizeCell's ^-anchored test in download.ts:18, so a formula-leading cell reaches buddies.csv and the clipboard with no apostrophe. Note the inversion in that regex: the only characters it covers beyond =+-@ are \t and \r, which import already refuses outright, so those branches are dead -- while the class that can actually get through is uncovered. Spreadsheet formula EXECUTION is not demonstrated (a name cannot contain a comma, and Excel keys detection on the literal first character), so leg (4) is forward-looking; legs (1)-(3) are reproduced today.
failure: importGraph({version:1, people:[{id:0,name:"Alice"},{id:1,name:"Alice​"},{id:2,name:"​"},{id:3,name:"Bob‮drowssap"}], edges:[[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[0,3]]}) is ACCEPTED. Resulting view.names === ["Alice","Alice​","​","Bob‮drowssap"]: the buddy list shows two rows both reading "Alice", one row with a blank name, and buddyLabel(view,0) === "Alice​, Bob‮drowssap" -- one DOM text node whose RLO reverses the tail. Separately, importGraph({version:1, people:[{id:0,name:"=cmd|'/c calc'!A0"},{id:1,name:"B"},{id:2,name:"C"}], edges:[[0,1],[1,2],[0,2]]}) is accepted and toCsv emits `"=cmd|'/c calc'!A0"` -- no leading apostrophe, because neutralizeCell's /^[=+\-@\t\r]/ sees U+0085, not '='. An exhaustive sweep of code points 0..0x3000 found 71 such leading characters (U+0080-U+009F, U+00AD, U+0600-U+0605, U+061C, U+06DD, U+070F, U+0890-U+0891, U+08E2, U+180E, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F).
remediation: Replace both hand-written ranges with a Unicode-category class: in importGraph.ts use `/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/u` for CONTROL_CHARS_TEST (refuse, matching the file's refuse-what-we-cannot-round-trip stance), and in parseRoster.ts use `/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/gu` for CONTROL_CHARS (normalize to space, matching the tolerant parser's contract). That single change makes legs (1)-(4) unreachable at once, and keeps the two authorities' round-trip agreement. Independently harden the sink: in download.ts anchor the test after leading non-graphic characters, e.g. `/^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Zs}]*[=+\-@]/u`, so neutralizeCell stays correct for any future producer that does not go through importGraph.
invariant: For every GraphView the app can hold, and for every string passed to toCsv or copyText: the string contains no code point in Unicode general category Cc or Cf; it is non-empty after removing all code points in Cc, Cf and Zs; the case-insensitive keys of view.names computed after that removal are pairwise distinct; and after removing any leading Cc/Cf/Zs code points the string does not begin with '=', '+', '-' or '@'.

theme: Inconsistent implementation pattern for similar operations
summary: Array equality check functions use different implementations inconsistently
failure: sameStrings (line 7-9) uses .every() for array equality, while sameEdges (line 11-17) uses a manual for loop. Both perform identical operations (element-by-element comparison) but with different code patterns.
remediation: Standardize on one implementation. Either: (1) rewrite sameEdges to use .every() for consistency with sameStrings, or (2) rewrite sameStrings to use a for loop like sameEdges. Recommend .every() as the more idiomatic React pattern and more concise. A contributor adding sameConstraints would have no consistent model to follow.
invariant: Array equality checks that compare two arrays for identical element sequences must use the same implementation pattern across the codebase to avoid confusion when similar functions are added.

theme: Comment phrasing creates ambiguity about the data flow and timing
summary: Comment about minSeparation and buddies 'becoming generation targets' is unclear about when and how
failure: Line 43-47 states: 'buddies' and 'minSeparation' become generation targets a later reroll passes to the core, so both are CLAMPED...'. The phrase 'become generation targets' is vague and could mislead a contributor about the flow: does this mean they are targets for the CURRENT generation, or targets FOR A LATER reroll? A new contributor reading this needs to understand that these values are clamped when imported, then stored in view.settings, then used in any subsequent reroll. The comment obscures this flow.
remediation: Replace 'become generation targets a later reroll passes to the core' with more specific language: 'are stored in Settings and may be used in later rerolls, so they must be CLAMPED to the range the UI can express'. This makes clear: (1) they are stored, not immediately used, (2) they may be used later, (3) the clamping is preventative for untrusted input that might get rerolled later.
invariant: Comments describing configuration flow must unambiguously indicate whether values are used immediately (current operation) or deferred (future operations), to prevent contributors from misunderstanding when clamping constraints apply.

theme: an element is removed from the DOM while it holds keyboard focus, and nothing redirects focus, so it silently falls to <body> and the next Tab restarts the whole page
summary: Notice's dismiss button is wired straight to `clear` (App.tsx:391, `<Notice message={notice} onDismiss={clear} />`) instead of through App's own `closeWithFocus`/`dismissOverlay` rescue helpers that every other self-closing panel in the app uses. A keyboard user who Tabs to the toast and presses Enter/Space removes the button (the ternary in Notice.tsx unmounts it once `message` is null) while it is the focused element, and focus is dropped on `<body>`.
failure: Reproduced directly: dispatch a generation, drive `hooks.state.status = 'error'` to raise a toast, `toast.focus()`, `fireEvent.click(toast)` (equivalent to Enter/Space) -> `document.activeElement === document.body` is true. The next Tab press then restarts from the top of the document (the '↻ Different arrangement' button), exactly the 'thrown back to the header' failure the file's own comments describe fixing for the person/route panels and both overlays — but the fix was never applied to Notice itself. Worse, the same removal also happens with NO user action at all: `useNotice.ts`'s `flash()` auto-clears after `AUTO_CLEAR_MS` (4000ms), so a user who tabs to the toast to read it slowly and doesn't act within 4s has focus pulled out from under them by a timer.
remediation: Route Notice's dismiss through the same focus-rescue pattern App.tsx already has (e.g. call closeWithFocus-style logic with a stable anchor such as searchRef, or simply .focus() a known-good element such as the search box / roster field) whenever the toast is dismissed by button, and also when the auto-clear timer fires while the toast holds focus.
invariant: For every element that can be unmounted or hidden by application code while it holds document.activeElement, some other visible non-inert element must receive focus in the same tick/microtask — document.activeElement must never settle on document.body as a result of an app-triggered removal.

theme: an element is removed from the DOM while it holds keyboard focus, and nothing redirects focus, so it silently falls to <body> and the next Tab restarts the whole page
summary: Choosing a search result via `choose()` (PersonSearch.tsx:42-46) clears `query`, which makes `open` false and unmounts the whole `role="listbox"` result list — including whichever `<button role="option">` was just interacted with. The keyboard path (Enter on the input, PersonSearch.tsx:57-61) never moves focus off the input so it is unaffected, but the pointer/hybrid path — clicking a result button directly — leaves the just-clicked button as `document.activeElement` at the moment it is unmounted.
failure: Reproduced directly: render App, generate a roster, type 'ali' into the search box, `screen.getByRole('option', {name: /alice/i})`, `.focus()` it, `fireEvent.click(option)` -> `document.activeElement` is `<body>` (`tagName === 'BODY'`) immediately after. Any user who reaches the option by pointer/touch (or via a screen-reader's virtual cursor click-equivalent) and then continues by keyboard restarts Tab from the top of the document instead of continuing from the search UI.
remediation: After `choose()` runs, explicitly return focus to the search input (`inputRef`/the input itself) rather than relying on the option button staying mounted.
invariant: For every element that can be unmounted or hidden by application code while it holds document.activeElement, some other visible non-inert element must receive focus in the same tick/microtask — document.activeElement must never settle on document.body as a result of an app-triggered removal.

theme: a control's numeric/stateful value changes visually with no accessible-tree counterpart, so a screen-reader user gets no feedback that their action did anything
summary: The 'Buddies each' stepper (SettingsControls.tsx:29-33) is two `
failure: A screen-reader user presses '+' repeatedly on the stepper; each press changes the visible digit in `.val` but nothing in the accessible tree changes on the currently-focused button (whose label stays 'more buddies'), so no announcement occurs and the user cannot tell how many buddies-per-person is currently set without leaving the button to inspect the page some other way.
remediation: Give the value an `aria-live="polite"` region (or better, mark the stepper as `role="group"` with a live `aria-valuenow`/visually-hidden text appended to each button's accessible name, e.g. `aria-label={`more buddies, currently ${settings.buddies}`}`), matching the pattern the app already uses for LayoutToggle's active state.
invariant: Every control whose activation changes an application-visible numeric/textual value must expose that new value somewhere in the accessible tree (a live region, an updated accessible name, or aria-valuenow) in the same update — a value change with no accessible counterpart must not occur.

theme: Function name does not fully describe all its responsibilities
summary: The 'quote' function handles three concerns but the name captures only one
failure: The function `quote` (line 17-19) is named as if it only performs quoting (JSON.stringify), but actually: (1) truncates input to max chars, (2) handles the truncation with an ellipsis, (3) serializes to JSON. A contributor reading 'quote(someValue)' would not expect truncation behavior. At line 18, it explicitly slices and appends '…' before calling JSON.stringify, making truncation a first-class responsibility, not an implementation detail.
remediation: Rename to `quoteTruncated` or `quoteAndTruncate` to explicitly advertise that truncation happens. Or, if brevity is preferred and the function is only used in this file (it is), add a JSDoc comment: '/** Truncate to max chars and JSON.stringify, for safe untrusted-data interpolation in error messages */'
invariant: Public and module-exported utility functions must have names that accurately reflect all their visible behavioral effects, especially when those effects (like truncation) affect the correctness of the result and might be unexpected to callers.

theme: an element is removed from the DOM while it holds keyboard focus, and nothing redirects focus, so it silently falls to <body> and the next Tab restarts the whole page
summary: The effect that reacts to `bg.status === 'refused' | 'error'` (App.tsx:156-172) reopens RosterModal (`setModalOpen(true)`) whenever a mid-session generation is refused or errors — e.g. a keyboard reroll dispatched from the '↻ Different arrangement' button, or 'Edit people' -> Generate on an existing view. Setting `modalOpen` true immediately makes `#app` `inert` (App.tsx:281), and per the HTML spec an element that becomes inert while focused is forcibly blurred with no automatic refocus; RosterModal itself has no `autoFocus` and the reopening effect never calls `.focus()` on anything inside it (grepped app/src for `autoFocus`/`.focus()` — the only `.focus()` calls are in `closeWithFocus`/`dismissOverlay`, neither of which this effect goes through). So the control the user was just on (e.g. the reroll button) is blurred with nothing rescuing focus, and the reopened dialog receives no focus either.
failure: Could not reproduce the blur itself in jsdom — jsdom does not implement `inert`'s focus-eviction behaviour (the existing test `appErrorRecovery.test.tsx` notes this explicitly: "jsdom does not implement inert's focus behaviour"). A scratch test driving `hooks.state.status = 'refused'` after focusing the reroll button left `document.activeElement` unchanged in jsdom, which is jsdom's known gap, not evidence the app is safe in a real browser. The code path — `#app inert={modalOpen}` toggling true with no compensating focus call anywhere in the refused/error branch — matches exactly the pattern the file's own comments (lines 80-127) describe fixing for every OTHER modalOpen transition (user-initiated ones, via dismissOverlay), but this is the one modalOpen transition that is NOT user-initiated and is not wrapped.
remediation: In the `bg.status === 'refused' | 'error'` effect, after `setModalOpen(true)`, move focus into the reopened dialog (e.g. focus its heading or first field, matching the ARIA APG dialog pattern) the same way dismissOverlay rescues focus for the user-initiated closes.
invariant: For every element that can be unmounted, hidden, or made inert by application code while it holds document.activeElement, some other visible non-inert element must receive focus in the same tick/microtask — document.activeElement must never settle on document.body (or on an element that has just become unfocusable) as a result of an app-triggered state change.

theme: the buddy count the organizer asked for can be silently not delivered, and the shortfall is presented as an optimal result
summary: When the core delivers fewer buddies per person than the requested k (routine at small n because the default minSeparation=5 forces the demotion floor), nothing in the UI says so — and because quality is scored against the DELIVERED degree, the gauge reads 100, isOptimal() is true, and a re-roll flashes "That's already an optimal arrangement". The app holds both numbers (settings.buddies and metrics.degreeMax) and never compares them.
failure: Reproduced through the real worker body + viewFromResult: roster of 6 names at the DEFAULT settings (buddies=4, polish auto, seed 12345) yields degreeMin=degreeMax=3. The stepper still reads 4, the rail reads "6 people · 3 buddies each", QualityPanel's gauge reads 100 and its caption reads "everyone's well-linked for 3 buddies each", and clicking "Different arrangement" flashes "That's already an optimal arrangement — a re-roll can't improve it" (App.tsx:39, isOptimal===true). Worse at n=8,k=7 -> 3-regular, q=100, opt=true; n=12,k=8 -> 4-regular, q=100, opt=true; n=9,k=5 -> 3–4, q=93. The ask is not impossible: the same n=8,k=7 with minSeparation=2 delivers a 7-regular graph, so a settings change the app never suggests would satisfy the request. No message anywhere states that the target was not met.
remediation: Derive the shortfall in the one display seam (model.ts) — e.g. a `targetShortfall(view)` returning non-null exactly when `metrics.degreeMax < settings.buddies` — and (a) render it in QualityPanel/the rail ("you asked for 4 buddies each; this arrangement gives 3 — try lowering Min separation in Advanced"), and (b) suppress the unqualified "already an optimal arrangement" copy in App.tsx:39 when it is non-null, wording it as optimal *for the buddy count actually delivered*. Do not change the scoring itself; scoring against degreeMax is deliberate and documented.
invariant: For every GraphView the app renders, if metrics.degreeMax < settings.buddies then the rendered output must contain a statement of the shortfall, and no unqualified optimality claim (the "already an optimal arrangement" copy) may be emitted; equivalently, a pure predicate shortfall(view) !== null must hold if and only if metrics.degreeMax < settings.buddies, and every optimality-claiming string must be gated on shortfall(view) === null.

theme: a per-person buddy count stated in prose is taken from the maximum degree, so it is false for most people on a non-regular graph
summary: connectionSummary names the yardstick using metrics.degreeMax alone (`${m.degreeMax} buddies each`), while the rail one panel away renders degreeLabel(m), which is a min–max range when the graph is not regular. The same view therefore states two different per-person buddy counts, and the prose one is the count only the maximum-degree person actually has.
failure: Reproduced: n=9, k=5 at default settings gives degreeMin=3, degreeMax=4. The rail renders "9 people · 3–4 buddies each" while QualityPanel renders "everyone's well-linked for 4 buddies each" — 8 of the 9 people have 3. Same at n=5/k=3 and n=13/k=3 ("for 3 buddies each" with degrees 2–3), which is the ordinary odd-n·k case the feasibility panel itself warns about, so it is not an edge case.
remediation: Have connectionSummary build its `per` clause from the same degreeLabel(m) the rail uses (e.g. "well-linked for 3–4 buddies each"), so one function owns the per-person buddy-count phrasing and the two panels cannot state different counts for one view.
invariant: For every Metrics value, the buddy-count token embedded in connectionSummary(m) must be exactly degreeLabel(m) — i.e. connectionSummary(m).includes(degreeLabel(m)) whenever it names a per-person buddy count — so no rendered surface states a per-person count that differs from the one the rail shows.

theme: untrusted names reach the render and spreadsheet sinks still carrying line-break characters, because the guard that claims to strip "line breaks" is keyed on the wrong Unicode categories
summary: Both name guards — importGraph's CONTROL_CHARS_TEST (importGraph.ts:24) and parseRoster's CONTROL_CHARS (parseRoster.ts:37) — match /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/u. U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR are categories Zl and Zp, so neither guard sees them, yet both are ECMAScript LineTerminators and CSS mandatory forced line breaks. The comment on importGraph.ts:18-23 says the class was widened from a hand-written C0+DEL range to Unicode CATEGORIES precisely so nothing named 'line break' could slip through; the two characters actually named 'line separator' and 'paragraph separator' still do, while the rejection message promises to refuse 'a tab, line break, or other control character'. The same characters also survive the parseRoster round-trip check that importGraph relies on as its authority, because trim() only removes them when they are leading or trailing.
failure: A JSON file containing {"version":1,"people":[{"id":0,"name":"Alice =cmd|'/c calc'!A1"},{"id":1,"name":"Zed"}],"edges":[[0,1]],...} is ACCEPTED by importGraph verbatim (reproduced: import returns names[0] === "Alice =cmd|'/c calc'!A1"). parseRoster("Alice =cmd|'/c calc'!A1") likewise returns the string unchanged, so the round-trip guard agrees. The name then reaches both spreadsheet-bound sinks intact: toCsv emits the cell "Alice =cmd|'/c calc'!A1" and BuddyList.copyAll emits the clipboard line "Alice =cmd|'/c calc'!A1: Zed". U+0085 NEL, U+000B and U+001C in the same position are all correctly refused — only the Zl/Zp pair gets through. Downstream, CSS Text treats U+2028 as a forced break in all white-space values, so one imported name renders as two lines in the buddy list row, the person panel heading and the printed slip.
remediation: Widen the shared character class in both authorities to include the separator categories that are line breaks: /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}]/u. Better, define the class ONCE and have both files import it — the two copies are already stated to be deliberate mirrors (refuse vs. normalize), and this defect is exactly a divergence that a single source would have made impossible to introduce in one place only. Add a case to the existing parseRoster/importGraph guard tests asserting the property below over the category set rather than over a list of characters.
invariant: For every string s: if importGraph accepts a file containing s as a name, or parseRoster returns s in names, then /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}]/u.test(s) === false. Equivalently: the character class used by importGraph's refusal and by parseRoster's normalization must be the same expression, and that expression must match every Unicode code point for which the character is a mandatory line break or a control/format character.

theme: a cost budget bounds the cheap half of an operation and nothing bounds the expensive half that immediately follows it
summary: layout.ts guards the synchronous force settle with three separate budgets — FORCE_MAX_N, FORCE_MAX_EDGES, and forceIters(n), whose whole documented purpose (layout.ts:396-414) is to hold the main-thread cost to a few hundred ms at the roster ceiling. The RAF interpolation in GraphCanvas that immediately consumes that settle has no size gate of any kind: on a layout toggle at a stable size with motion allowed, `step` calls setDisplay(to.map(...)) once per frame for 650 ms, and each setDisplay re-renders every one of the n node groups (4 SVG elements each) and every one of the m <line> elements. So a 300 ms bounded settle is followed by roughly 60 unbounded full re-renders of the same data. reducedMotion() is the only escape, and it is a user preference, not a bound. The cheap-vs-expensive asymmetry is the defect: the gate was placed on the half that was already the smaller cost.
failure: Import a file with 1000 people and 6000 edges (a 12-regular circulant — it passes the density gate at exactly 2m = BUDDY_MAX*n and the per-vertex degree gate at exactly 12), then press the ring/force layout toggle. Measured with @testing-library/react under jsdom: one full GraphCanvas render at n=1000/m=6000 costs 346 ms and produces 10 001 SVG elements; App re-renders the unmemoized BuddyList and Slips alongside it for a further ~180 ms over 7 012 more DOM nodes. The animation requests ~60 such frames inside a 650 ms window. forceLayout itself, by contrast, measured 299 ms once. jsdom overstates absolute DOM cost relative to a browser, so the per-frame wall clock in Chrome will be lower — the structural claim (per-frame work scales with n and m, with no threshold above which the animation is skipped) is traced directly in the code at GraphCanvas.tsx:601-617 and does not depend on the measurement.
remediation: Give the animation the same kind of gate the settle already has. Add the size test to the existing snap condition at GraphCanvas.tsx:601, e.g. `if (sizeChanged || !layoutChanged || reducedMotion() || from.length !== to.length || n > ANIM_MAX_N || edges.length > ANIM_MAX_EDGES) { setDisplay(to); return; }`, with ANIM_MAX_N/ANIM_MAX_EDGES exported from layout.ts beside FORCE_MAX_N/FORCE_MAX_EDGES so the two budgets are stated together and the existing cost-budget test can assert both. Above the threshold the toggle snaps, which is exactly what it already does for a reduced-motion user and for a size change.
invariant: For every (n, edges) GraphCanvas can be mounted with, the number of times setDisplay is called in response to a single layout toggle is 1 whenever n or edges.length exceeds the declared animation budget — i.e. no requestAnimationFrame is scheduled above the threshold. Machine-checkable: with fake timers and a spy on requestAnimationFrame, render at a size above the budget, change `layout`, and assert requestAnimationFrame was never called; below the budget assert it was.

theme: the import re-check path computes a value the metrics path already computed, instead of sharing it
summary: Implementing the constraints re-check follow-on the way the core's existing report-building function is shaped naturally leads to computing largestComponentFraction(g) twice per constrained import: once explicitly for GraphView.metrics.largestComponentFraction (importGraph.ts, final return), and again inside the core's buildReport (invoked via the new checkConstraints wrapper) because ConstraintReport carries its own largestComponentFraction field. The generation path (app/src/worker/generate.ts fromConstrained) already avoids this exact duplication by reading `r.report.largestComponentFraction` straight into GraphResult instead of recomputing it — so the pattern to avoid it already exists in the codebase, just not reachable from the import path since import computes its own summary independently of any report.
failure: For a large, dense, constrained import near the MAX_IMPORT_N=1000 / density-cap ceiling, largestComponentFraction's O(n+m) connected-components walk runs twice on the identical graph where the generate.ts path runs it once — cheap in absolute terms (bounded by the same caps that already bound the rest of import), but it is duplicated work with no caller-visible benefit, and the two results could in principle be read as independently-sourced when they are guaranteed-identical by construction.
remediation: When constraints are present, take metrics.largestComponentFraction from report.largestComponentFraction (mirroring generate.ts's fromConstrained) instead of calling largestComponentFraction(g) a second time; when constraints are absent there is only one call already.
invariant: for a given import call, largestComponentFraction(g) is invoked at most once for a given Graph g

theme: an aria-live/role=status container is created in the very same render as the text it first announces, instead of already existing in the DOM before the content changes
summary: The busy overlay (`Generating…`) is only rendered while `bg.status === "running"`, so its `role="status" aria-live="polite"` container and its text `Generating…` are both inserted into the DOM in the same commit. Notice.tsx's own doc comment identifies exactly this pattern as unreliable and keeps its region permanently mounted for that reason (`app/src/panels/Notice.tsx:9-11`), but App.tsx's busy overlay was not built the same way. At the same moment the region (dis)appears, `#app` also goes `inert`, removing every other control from the tree — so a screen-reader user who doesn't hear the freshly-mounted announcement has no signal that anything happened, and the controls they were just on have gone silent.
failure: Generate a graph, press "Different arrangement" (or trigger any generation) with a screen reader running: because the `.busy` node with `role="status"` is created at the same instant its text content is set, many AT/browser combinations (e.g. JAWS+Chrome) do not announce "Generating…" reliably — unlike a message written into an already-mounted region (Notice), which is designed to announce reliably.
remediation: Render the busy region unconditionally (like Notice) and toggle only its text content between `null`/empty and "Generating…", instead of conditionally mounting the whole `<div className="busy">...` on `bg.status === "running"`.
invariant: Every element carrying `aria-live`/`role="status"` must already exist in a DOM commit prior to the render that first supplies its non-empty announced text; the container's own mount and the arrival of its first text must not be the same commit.

theme: an aria-live/role=status container is created in the very same render as the text it first announces, instead of already existing in the DOM before the content changes
summary:
PathPanel itself (and its `

The comment above the `

` explains why a live region must pre-exist its content, but only within the panel; the panel's own conditional mount reproduces the problem one level up.
failure: Select a person, press "Find a path from here": a screen-reader user may not hear "Starting from X — now pick the other person" because the region was created with that text already inside it rather than updated after it existed.
remediation: Keep a persistent path-status live region mounted whenever a graph view exists (mirroring Notice's always-mounted toast region), or mount PathPanel eagerly with an empty body and only populate `from`/`route` a tick later.
